subject: Coordination: acceptance sprint, MAP milestones & billing options for LuminaTech
messages:

Subject: Re: Coordination for private offer & billing path

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has asked us to put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) so we can lock timelines for evaluation and the purchase path (GCP private offer). Two quick asks from our side:

1) Can Redwood compress the evaluation window to two weeks (we have a constrained pilot budget)?
2) Our procurement team prefers a marketplace private offer but needs clarity on invoice flow: do we get monthly invoices from Redwood or handle billing via GCP invoice? Any alternative: Net30 invoices vs PO on the marketplace?

I'm attaching the procurement questionnaire they asked us to start with. Samir (CC) is procurement lead and will own getting POs in place.

Attachments: procurement_questionnaire.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

Appreciate a short mutual action plan we can share with legal/procurement.

—Claire

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-30T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Coordination for private offer & billing path

Claire —

Thanks for the questionnaire — very helpful. I've put together a concise MAP draft and an acceptance sprint that we can compress into two weeks if LuminaTech can commit to the evaluation criteria up front. See the high-level plan below and attached draft MAP (LuminaTech_MAP-draft.pdf).

High-level MAP (draft):
- Week 0 (kickoff): finalize scope, enable test accounts (private offer sandbox), confirm KMS/access controls (day 1).
- Week 1 (functional eval): run a predefined prompt/eval set (we'll provide prompt templates + metrics); Redwood provides 3-day tech support window and 24-hr SLA for urgent infra issues.
- Week 2 (acceptance & sign): joint review, sign SOW / finalize private offer terms, hand-off to billing/procurement.

Acceptance criteria (short):
- End-to-end integration in private offer sandbox with sample inference throughput >= 10 req/s for 512-length requests.
- No unresolved P1/P2 infra bugs; model outputs pass basic quality regression threshold (we will provide the eval pass/fail sheet).

Billing paths we support (options):
A) Marketplace private offer (recommended): LuminaTech accepts a GCP private offer; billing flows through GCP and Redwood invoices are handled as marketplace line items. This is simplest for procurement but may require GCP PO alignment.
B) Direct invoice (Net30): Redwood issues monthly invoices to LuminaTech under a short-term SOW while private offer is finalized. Good fallback if your procurement needs Net30 terms.
C) Hybrid: initial month via direct invoice, then migrate to marketplace billing on activation.

Next steps for LuminaTech: confirm preferred billing path (A/B/C) and whether procurement can commit to signing within 48 hours of acceptance. If so, we'll prepare SOW and DocuSign link.

Attachments: LuminaTech_MAP-draft.pdf, SOW_draft.docx

Thanks — I looped Karthik for the private-offer setup and Ben for billing/invoice routing.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, North America
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Claire Adams <claire.adams@luminatech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-12-01T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Coordination for private offer & billing path

Claire / Marissa —

Quick technical note on the GCP private offer acceptance sprint: we can support the compressed 2-week window but need the following from LuminaTech on day 0 to avoid delays:
- Access: a test billing account/project with private offer sandbox permission (or invite us as marketplace vendor tester).
- Keys: KMS key policy requirements (if you require customer-managed keys we need the KMS fingerprint and IAM role mapping).
- Test vectors: your top 20 prompts and a small set of production-ish examples so we can run quality regression locally.

Operationally we will:
- Provision a private-offer sandbox within 48 hours.
- Reserve a small GPU pool for benchmarking during week 1.
- Provide a short acceptance checklist and a final CSV of eval results.

Billing clarification from my side: if you choose Marketplace private offer, the actual money movement is through GCP (GCP invoices LuminaTech) but Redwood can issue a reconciliation invoice or monthly usage summary. If procurement needs a standalone Net30 invoice, Ben can send one for the first invoice cycle.

On KMS: if LuminaTech requires a customer-managed key in GCP, that is supported but will add a 1–2 day setup to the kickoff timeline.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Marketplace Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Adams <claire.adams@luminatech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@luminatech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-12-03T16:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Coordination for private offer & billing path

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks, that level of detail is great. Procurement is amenable to the two-week sprint provided we compress approvals. Two clarifications:

1) Can Redwood accept a conditional PO issued by LuminaTech that converts to Marketplace private offer on activation? Procurement prefers the bookkeeping to show a PO number up front (even if invoicing migrates to GCP).
2) If we need CMK (customer-managed key) on day 0, we will request it; can you confirm whether that will push accept by >48 hours?

Samir will be our procurement contact on the PO logistics. He prefers the hybrid billing path (C) — start with a Net30 invoice for month 0 and flip to Marketplace on activation.

If you can update the MAP with those two items and share a DocuSign SOW we can get legal/procurement signatures quickly.

—Claire
Claire Adams
Head of Platform Partnerships
LuminaTech
